findings.title: Unauthorized access via support mode header
findings.problem: The authorize function allows any user to bypass authorization checks if they provide the 'x-support-mode' header set to '1'.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove the hardcoded support mode check. Implement a secure, authenticated support mechanism if needed.

findings.title: Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in inventory reservation
findings.problem: The inventory reservation logic reads the stock level and then updates it in two separate asynchronous operations without locking, allowing race conditions.
findings.recommendedFix: Use database-level transactions with appropriate locking (e.g., SELECT FOR UPDATE) or atomic decrement operations within the database.

findings.title: N+1 query problem in listUsers
findings.problem: The listUsers function performs an N+1 query pattern by executing a separate SQL query for every user to fetch their profile within a map/Promise.all loop.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a single SQL JOIN query or fetch all profiles for the list of users in a single 'WHERE user_id IN (...)' query.

evidence.text: return Promise.all(users.map(async (user) => ({ ...user, profile: (await db.query("SELECT * FROM profiles WHERE user_id = $1", [user.id]))[0] })));

findings.title: Redundant payment capture logic with potential side effects
findings.problem: The catch block retries the payment capture exactly as it was called in the try block without error handling, which could lead to double-charging or idempotency issues if the gateway is not idempotent.
findings.recommendedFix: Ensure the payment gateway integration supports idempotency keys or implement proper error handling that prevents blind retries.

evidence.text:
try { await gateway.capture(paymentId, amount); }
  catch { await gateway.capture(paymentId, amount); }
